blocks.html: San Luis Fishing Guide — San Jose del Cabo
Discover San Luis fishing near San Jose del Cabo: snapper, grouper, yellowfin tuna and roosterfish along nearby coastal fishing grounds and rocky structure.

San Luis is an interesting fishing area northeast of San Jose del Cabo, combining opportunities around rocky bottom structures with nearby coastal waters where roosterfish, jacks and other seasonal species have been reported.

Unlike fishing grounds discussed primarily in connection with offshore yellowfin tuna, San Luis appears in regional reports covering several styles of fishing.

These include drifting bait for tuna, jigging or bottom fishing around structure, and exploring the shoreline with live bait.

The result is a versatile area whose opportunities depend strongly on conditions and target species.

Where Is San Luis Fishing Ground?

San Luis is located along the Sea of Cortez fishing grounds northeast of Puerto Los Cabos Marina.

Regional fishing reports refer both to rocky bottom structures around San Luis and to the surrounding shoreline.

These are important distinctions.

The fishing techniques used for snapper and grouper around bottom structure differ from those used for roosterfish along the coast.

San Luis is frequently discussed alongside Iman Bank and Vinorama because these locations can offer different fishing opportunities depending on bait and ocean conditions.

Snapper and Grouper — Fishing the Rocky Structure

Bottom fishing is one of the strongest documented opportunities around San Luis.

In September 2026, a regional report described the best fishing activity at the bottom structures of San Luis and Iman Bank while yellowfin tuna fishing remained slow.

Reported species across those two areas included:

  • Dogtooth snapper

  • Barred snapper

  • Mullet snapper

  • Grouper

  • Triggerfish

Chunks of skipjack were used for much of the bottom fishing, while sardines also produced smaller snapper.

A February 2026 report documented amberjack, grouper and a variety of snapper around Vinorama and San Luis during a short period of productive fishing.

Some of the fish responded to vertical jigs, while others were taken on bait.

These observations suggest that San Luis can provide a useful alternative when anglers are not finding active yellowfin tuna.

However, bottom fishing can become difficult when currents are strong.

Roosterfish — A Highlight Along the San Luis Shoreline

Roosterfish are a distinctive part of the coastal fishing opportunities associated with San Luis.

During June and July 2026, regional reports described roosterfish activity along the shorelines around San Luis.

Some fish were reported in the 30–50-pound range, with larger roosterfish becoming less common as July progressed.

Live caballito and green jacks were among the baits used while fishing nearby shorelines and rocky areas.

These historical reports show why San Luis can be relevant to anglers interested in an inshore fishing experience.

However, roosterfish catches vary seasonally and should never be treated as guaranteed.

Yellowfin Tuna — Opportunities Beyond the Bottom Structure

Yellowfin tuna are also documented in the waters around San Luis.

A May 2026 regional report described tuna activity at Vinorama and San Luis using live sardines, followed by significant shark interference.

During February 2026, yellowfin tuna were reported around the same general fishing grounds, alongside amberjack, grouper and snapper.

A June 2026 report also described tuna encounters near San Luis, including fish associated with offshore porpoise activity.

These observations show that San Luis may be relevant for more than bottom fishing.

However, tuna activity can be unpredictable, and the most productive ground may change from one day to the next.

Amberjack, Jacks and Other Coastal Species

Regional reports have also documented amberjack and other jacks around the San Luis fishing area.

Amberjack may be targeted around rocky structure using bait or jigs.

Closer to shore, anglers may encounter jacks and other seasonal species while presenting live bait.

The fishing method should be selected according to the actual location and species being targeted.

An outing dedicated to roosterfish along the shoreline is not the same as a bottom-fishing session over deeper structure.

Fishing Techniques Around San Luis

Different approaches can be useful depending on the goal:

  • Drifting chunks of bait: For snapper, grouper and other bottom-associated species.

  • Vertical jigging: For amberjack and fish holding around rocky structure.

  • Live sardines: Used for yellowfin tuna and some bottom-fishing opportunities.

  • Slow trolling live caballito or green jacks: Used along the shoreline when targeting roosterfish and other coastal predators.

  • Moving between fishing areas: An option when currents, sharks or changing fish activity make the original plan less productive.

The best strategy depends on recent reports and the conditions encountered during the outing.

When Is San Luis Worth Fishing?

San Luis may be worth considering when anglers want to combine fishing possibilities rather than concentrate exclusively on a single offshore species.

Historical reports document:

  • Late winter: Tuna, snapper, grouper and amberjack activity in the broader Vinorama–San Luis area.

  • Late spring and early summer: Yellowfin tuna opportunities and documented roosterfish activity along the shoreline.

  • Early fall: Productive bottom-fishing opportunities at San Luis and Iman when the tuna bite was inconsistent.

These observations do not establish a guaranteed seasonal calendar. They illustrate how fishing opportunities can change during the year.

San Luis vs. Vinorama and Iman Bank

Vinorama is frequently discussed in connection with yellowfin tuna fishing.

Iman Bank has documented opportunities for tuna and several bottom-dwelling species.

San Luis offers an additional combination of rocky structure and accessible coastal fishing areas.

For anglers who value flexibility, this variety may make San Luis one of several locations to consider while planning a private fishing charter.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you catch roosterfish around San Luis?

Yes. Historical regional reports document roosterfish along the San Luis shoreline, particularly during late spring and early summer.

Is San Luis good for snapper and grouper?

Regional reports include snapper and grouper around San Luis and nearby bottom structures. Results depend on currents, bait and fish activity.

Is San Luis an offshore or inshore fishing area?

Regional reports describe both coastal fishing along the San Luis shoreline and fishing around deeper rocky structure. The approach depends on your target species.
